title: Biology · Paper 2 (HL) — original full-format practice
subject: biology
instructions: Answer every question using the response area attached to it. An approved calculator is required; all data needed for this original sample is supplied within DigitalDP. Show calculations, units, diagrams and reasoning where required. No separate answer sheet is used.

resources.label: Original pond study
resources.text: Researchers added equal masses of leaf litter to eight pond tanks. Four tanks received extra nitrate. After 21 days, mean algal dry mass was 3.8 g without nitrate and 9.6 g with nitrate. Mean dissolved oxygen at dawn was 7.2 mg L⁻¹ without nitrate and 3.9 mg L⁻¹ with nitrate.

questions.label: Question 1 — data interpretation
questions.prompt: Calculate the percentage increase in mean algal dry mass caused by nitrate. Show the calculation and state the answer to three significant figures.

questions.label: Question 2 — causal model
questions.prompt: Construct an annotated causal diagram linking added nitrate to the change in dissolved oxygen at dawn.

questions.label: Question 3 — experimental design
questions.prompt: Design a follow-up investigation to test whether light intensity changes the effect of nitrate on algal growth. Include variables, controls, replication and the data to be collected.

questions.label: Section A · Question 4 — membranes
questions.prompt: Explain how the properties of phospholipids and membrane proteins permit selective transport, using one passive and one active example.

questions.label: Section A · Question 5 — genetics
questions.prompt: A heterozygous individual for two unlinked genes is test-crossed. Construct the cross, predict the phenotypic ratio, and explain how linkage would alter the result.

questions.label: Section A · Question 6 — photosynthesis
questions.prompt: Outline how light energy is converted into chemical energy and used to produce carbohydrate. Distinguish events at the thylakoid from those in the stroma.

questions.label: Section A · Question 7 — homeostasis
questions.prompt: Explain how insulin and glucagon coordinate the response to a meal and a subsequent period without food.

questions.label: Section A · Question 8 — evolution
questions.prompt: Use natural selection to explain how resistance to a new antibiotic can become common in a bacterial population.

questions.label: Section B · choose two alternatives
questions.prompt:
Answer any two alternatives, writing a separate response for each.
A. Explain how gene expression is regulated and how cell differentiation can arise from a shared genome. [16]
B. Compare energy transfer and nutrient cycling in ecosystems, and evaluate one human intervention intended to improve sustainability. [16]
C. Explain how nervous and hormonal communication coordinate responses in mammals. [16]
